segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The recent conversation was the first thing that came to mind as a comparison point; it was the most vivid thing in my head, not necessarily the most similar case.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A recently discussed comparison case was overweighted over Participant 12's fuller record.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Possibly related kind of kicked the can down the road; I wanted something I could close out.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant avoided the intermediate category because it felt unresolved and burdensome.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The PI asked me to pull his full lab history and prior meds before finalizing it; I probably should have done that up front.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a substantive correction reflection without a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Twenty hours felt like too much to walk away from without one more push.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Continuation was justified by prior investment rather than forward-looking resolvability.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The 'losing a fifth of our population' framing stuck with me; it became about what we'd be giving up.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The loss-oriented wording changed evaluation of the continuation decision.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I put him lower in the queue because he probably wasn't going to qualify; it was more that he didn't match the pattern I'm used to seeing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Screening was deprioritized based on prototype mismatch rather than objective criteria.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: He met every inclusion criterion. Which doesn't tell you much either way about whether deprioritizing him was the right call.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant correctly limits retrospective inference from the outcome.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Most of the other sites had already moved to it, which made staying with our old method feel like we were behind; I did not look for validation data.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The shortcut was adopted because peer sites had adopted it despite absent validation data.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Four of six positive segments are detected at high confidence; both negative segments are correctly rejected.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Adding the moderate-confidence sunk-cost finding detects five of six positive segments with no false alarms.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All six positive segments are detected once the low-confidence ambiguity finding is included, with no false alarms.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: There are no candidates, so this threshold is identical to the all-identified threshold.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full overlap with the hidden recent-case weighting mechanism, but the taxonomy label emphasizes ease of recall rather than recency.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly states that no retrieved corpus passages were supplied and provides no citation metadata; corpus support is unavailable but not misrepresented.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding the moderate-confidence sunk-cost finding changes segment hits from 4 to 5 and strict instance TPs from 3 to 4; no false alarms are added.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Adding the low-confidence ambiguity finding changes segment hits from 5 to 6 and strict instance TPs from 4 to 5; no false alarms are added.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high-and-moderate threshold, 5/6 positive segments were detected with 0 false alarms (hit rate 0.8333; F1 0.9091). All six are detected when low-confidence findings are included.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At all identified confidence levels, 5/6 hidden instances are strict true positives (precision 0.8333; recall 0.8333; F1 0.8333); the recency instance is localized and mechanistically correct but mislabeled as availability heuristic.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At all identified confidence levels, all 6/6 hidden mechanisms are matched with no false positives (precision, recall, and F1 all 1.0000).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidate findings were produced, so the candidate tier adds no detections, errors, or threshold change.
main_failure_modes: One near-neighbor taxonomy error: availability heuristic was used instead of the hidden Recency Bias label.
Two correct findings are below the recommended high-and-moderate threshold: sunk cost is moderate and ambiguity aversion is low.
main_strengths: All six findings localize to the correct reasoning spans with valid interview quotations.
All six hidden mechanisms are captured at the mechanism-first scorecard.
No unsupported predictions, duplicate findings, fabricated quotations, or negative-segment false alarms were found.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run is strong on evidence-grounded mechanism detection and segment localization. The small strict-scorecard gap is attributable to one ontology-level near-neighbor label choice and confidence calibration, not to missing reasoning evidence.
